LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.titleEnglish: Send an Action to Someone with 給
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.learnerPromise: Show who receives a card, call, letter, or helpful action.
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.explanation: Put 給 before the person, then say the action. The action goes to that person.

lessonWorld.title: Send the action to someone
lessonWorld.prompt: Youmei writes a card to her new friend.
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gěi péngyǒu xiě kǎpiàn.
lessonWorld.english: I want to write a card to my friend.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

patternRows.english: I write a card to my friend.
Mom buys a gift for me.

items.question: “Write a card to a friend” — 給 or 跟?
items.answer: 給. The friend gets the card. 跟 goes with someone — like meeting or chatting together.

right.english: I write a card to my friend.

items.question: Where does the person who gets it go?
items.answer: Right after 給, before the action. 給 + person + action.

right.english: I write a card to my friend.

items.question: How do I say “my brother did not call me”?
items.answer: Put 給我 before 打電話. The person who gets the call comes right after 給.

right.pinyin: Gēge méi gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
right.english: My older brother did not call me.

discoveryLab.title: Follow the arrow to the person
discoveryLab.description: The action travels toward the person after 給.

choices.label: Friend
choices.english: I write a card to my friend.
choices.note: The friend gets the card.

choices.label: Me
choices.note: 我 gets the call.

choices.label: Mom
choices.english: I buy a gift for Mom.
choices.note: 媽媽 gets the gift.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Find who gets it. Put 給 right before that person.

examples.teachingNote: 她 gets the letter.

text.traditional: 我想給她寫信。
text.simplified: 我想给她写信。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gěi tā xiě xìn.
text.english: I want to write her a letter.

examples.teachingNote: Even after 沒, 給 stays before the person.

text.traditional: 哥哥沒給我打電話。
text.simplified: 哥哥没给我打电话。
text.pinyin: Gēge méi gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
text.english: My older brother did not call me.

examples.teachingNote: 我 gets the ice cream.

text.traditional: 媽媽給我買了冰淇淋。
text.simplified: 妈妈给我买了冰淇淋。
text.pinyin: Māma gěi wǒ mǎi le bīngqílín.
text.english: Mom bought me ice cream.

examples.teachingNote: You can use 還沒 and 給 together.

text.traditional: 你還沒給哥哥寫生日卡片嗎？
text.simplified: 你还没给哥哥写生日卡片吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ hái méi gěi gēge xiě shēngrì kǎpiàn ma?
text.english: Have you not written your brother a birthday card yet?

segments.hint: Build 給 + person + action.

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.titleEnglish: Put Steps in Order with 先…等…再…
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Explain a plan where you do one thing, wait, then do another.
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: 先 starts the first action. 等 names what you wait for. 再 starts the later action.

lessonWorld.title: Plan what happens next
lessonWorld.prompt: Youmei needs to decide, wait for a free time, and then arrange the meeting.
lessonWorld.traditional: 先決定，等朋友有空，再約時間。
lessonWorld.simplified: 先决定，等朋友有空，再约时间。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Xiān juédìng, děng péngyǒu yǒukòng, zài yuē shíjiān.
lessonWorld.english: Decide first, wait until the friend is free, then arrange a time.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.pattern: 先 + first action，等 + condition，再 + later action

patternRows.english: Do homework first; wait for Dad; then eat.
Practice first; wait for the teacher; then start class.
Decide first; wait for the friend; then call.

items.question: Which step does 先 start?
items.answer: 先 starts the first action. 等 names what you wait for, and 再 starts the later action.

right.pinyin: Xiān zuò gōngkè, zài kàn diànshì.
right.english: Do homework first, then watch TV.

items.question: Is it 在 or 再 for the later step?
items.answer: 再. It means “then; after that”. 在 talks about where something is.

right.english: Decide first, then arrange a time.

items.question: Can 再 start the first step?
items.answer: No. 再 belongs to the later action. 先 opens the plan.

discoveryLab.title: Build the three-stop timeline
discoveryLab.description: Do not jump to 再. Something must happen or become true after 等.

choices.label: Dinner
choices.traditional: 先做功課，等爸爸回家，再一起吃飯。
choices.simplified: 先做功课，等爸爸回家，再一起吃饭。
choices.pinyin: Xiān zuò gōngkè, děng bàba huí jiā, zài yìqǐ chīfàn.
choices.english: Do homework first, wait for Dad to return, then eat together.
choices.note: The middle event must happen first.

choices.label: Class
choices.traditional: 先練習，等老師來了，再上課。
choices.simplified: 先练习，等老师来了，再上课。
choices.pinyin: Xiān liànxí, děng lǎoshī lái le, zài shàngkè.
choices.english: Practice first, wait for the teacher, then begin class.
choices.note: 老師來 is what you wait for after 等.

choices.label: Call later
choices.traditional: 先想一想，等妳決定了，再給我打電話。
choices.simplified: 先想一想，等你决定了，再给我打电话。
choices.pinyin: Xiān xiǎng yì xiǎng, děng nǐ juédìng le, zài gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
choices.english: Think first; when you decide, call me.
choices.note: The call waits for the decision.

discoveryLab.takeaway: 先 starts it. 等 waits for it. 再 moves to the later action.

examples.teachingNote: The first step is left out; the wait is named.

text.traditional: 等她睡醒了，再跟她說。
text.simplified: 等她睡醒了，再跟她说。
text.pinyin: Děng tā shuìxǐng le, zài gēn tā shuō.
text.english: Wait until she wakes, then tell her.

examples.teachingNote: What you wait for comes after 等.

text.traditional: 天氣太冷了，等車來了，我們再出去。
text.simplified: 天气太冷了，等车来了，我们再出去。
text.pinyin: Tiānqì tài lěng le, děng chē lái le, wǒmen zài chūqù.
text.english: It is too cold; wait for the car, then go outside.

examples.teachingNote: All three stages appear.

text.traditional: 先做功課，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯。
text.simplified: 先做功课，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚饭。
text.pinyin: Xiān zuò gōngkè, děng bàba huí jiā le, zài yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn.
text.english: Do homework first; when Dad returns, eat dinner together.

examples.teachingNote: A fun example from the book.

text.traditional: 我們先吃冰淇淋，等不熱了，再去海邊玩。
text.simplified: 我们先吃冰淇淋，等不热了，再去海边玩。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān chī bīngqílín, děng bú rè le, zài qù hǎibiān wán.
text.english: Let us eat ice cream first, wait until it is cooler, then go to the beach.

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.exerciseInstruction: Complete the first, wait, and then sequence.

questions.correctFeedback: 先 starts the first action.

segments.hint: Use 等 before what you wait for.

questions.correctFeedback: 等 starts what you wait for.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 等 before what you wait for.

questions.repairFeedback: Use 再 for the later action.

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.learnerPromise: Say that an action is finished.
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.explanation: Put 了 after the action word to show it is finished. When talking about amounts (like “two cups” or “ten pages”), a single 了 means you stopped there, while two 了’s mean you reached that amount so far and may keep going.

lessonWorld.title: Rebuild the chat history
lessonWorld.prompt: Yiwen asks whether Youmei completed today’s homework.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

items.question: Where does 了 go in “I wrote the homework yesterday”?
items.answer: Right after the action word. 了 follows 寫, before the homework.

items.question: Do I need 了 for something I do every day?
items.answer: No. 了 marks one finished action. For a habit you repeat, leave 了 out.

items.question: How do I say “I am writing a card” right now?
items.answer: Use 在 before the action word. 了 would say the card is already done.

discoveryLab.title: Watch the action reach DONE
discoveryLab.description: The picture—not the English time words—shows whether the action is happening now or already finished.

choices.label: General action
choices.note: The sentence names the activity. It does not say if it is happening now or finished.

choices.label: Happening now
choices.note: 在 shows the action is happening now.

choices.label: Completed
choices.note: 了 shows the action is finished.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Ask: is the action general, happening now, or finished?

examples.teachingNote: Single 了 after V(O) indicates a completed action in the past.

text.traditional: 他已經去上課了。
text.simplified: 他已经去上课了。
text.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng qù shàngkè le.
text.english: He has already gone to class.

examples.teachingNote: 今天早上去看醫生了 indicates the visit is completed.

text.traditional: 我今天早上去看醫生了。
text.simplified: 我今天早上去看医生了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān zǎoshang qù kàn yīshēng le.
text.english: I went to see the doctor this morning.

examples.teachingNote: 都寫功課了 confirms the homework is finished.

text.traditional: 我跟弟弟都寫功課了。
text.simplified: 我跟弟弟都写功课了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn dìdi dōu xiě gōngkè le.
text.english: My younger brother and I have both finished our homework.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for past completed quantity; (b) Double 了 indicates so far, with more likely to come.

text.traditional: 我上個禮拜學了十個中國字。我已經學了四百多個中國字了。
text.simplified: 我上个礼拜学了十个中国字。我已经学了四百多个中国字了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ shàng ge lǐbài xué le shí ge Zhōngguózì. Wǒ yǐjīng xué le sìbǎi duō ge Zhōngguózì le.
text.english: I learned ten Chinese characters last week. I have already learned more than 400 Chinese characters so far.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for buying a car; (b) Double 了 indicates he already bought one and still wants another.

text.traditional: 爸爸上個月買了一輛新車。爸爸已經買了一輛新車了，還想再買一輛。
text.simplified: 爸爸上个月买了一辆新车。爸爸已经买了一辆新车了，还想再买一辆。
text.pinyin: Bàba shàng ge yuè mǎi le yí liàng xīn chē. Bàba yǐjīng mǎi le yí liàng xīn chē le, hái xiǎng zài mǎi yí liàng.
text.english: Dad bought a new car last month. Dad has already bought a new car, and he still wants to buy another one.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for eating two apples yesterday; (b) Double 了 indicates he ate one so far and wants more.

text.traditional: 他昨天晚上吃了兩個蘋果。他很愛吃蘋果，已經吃了一個了，還想再吃。
text.simplified: 他昨天晚上吃了两个苹果。他很爱吃苹果，已经吃了一个了，还想再吃。
text.pinyin: Tā zuótiān wǎnshang chī le liǎng ge píngguǒ. Tā hěn ài chī píngguǒ, yǐjīng chī le yí ge le, hái xiǎng zài chī.
text.english: He ate two apples yesterday evening. He loves eating apples; he has already eaten one and wants to eat more.

words.pinyin: yǐjīng chī le yí ge le

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.exercisePreview: Choose the form that shows the action is done.

segments.hint: Use 寫 + 了 + 功課.

questions.correctFeedback: 了 comes right after the action word.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 寫 + 了 + 功課.

segments.hint: Put 了 after 喝.

questions.correctFeedback: The finished action word is 喝了.

segments.hint: Put 了 after the action word, before the thing.

questions.correctFeedback: 買了 shows the event is done.
questions.repairFeedback: Put 了 after the action word, before the thing.

subsections.title: Completed Action (Action + 了)
subsections.explanation: Put 了 right after the action word or phrase to show it is done, like “he went to class” or “I saw the doctor.”

subsections.title: Counting Amounts: One 了 vs Two 了's
subsections.explanation: One 了 means the action finished in the past (“I drank two cups yesterday”). Two 了's mean you reached that number so far and might do more (“I have already drunk two cups, and want another”).

patternRows.english: I drank two cups of coffee yesterday (Single 了: completed in past).

complement.meaning: two cups of coffee so far

patternRows.english: I have already drunk two cups of coffee so far (Double 了: may continue).

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleTraditional: 把聚光燈放在過去的細節上
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleEnglish: Spotlight One Detail with 是…的
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.learnerPromise: Point out when, where, how, or with whom something happened.
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.explanation: The event is already known. 是…的 puts the spotlight on one detail: when, where, how, or with whom it happened.

lessonWorld.title: Rebuild the chat history
lessonWorld.prompt: Yiwen knows that Youmei met someone. She wants the missing detail.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.pattern: Person + 是 + focused detail + action + 的

items.question: “How did you meet?” — do I answer with 了?
items.answer: No. The question asks how, so 是…的 puts the spotlight on the way you met. 了 alone would only say it happened.

items.question: Where does the detail go in a 是…的 sentence?
items.answer: Between 是 and the action word. The way you met comes before 認識.

items.question: Do I need the 的 at the end?
items.answer: Yes. 是…的 works as a pair. Without the ending 的, the sentence loses its spotlight.

discoveryLab.title: Move the spotlight
discoveryLab.description: The event stays known. Change only the detail the listener wants.

choices.label: When
choices.pinyin: Wǒ shì zuótiān rènshi tā de.
choices.note: 昨天 is the detail in the spotlight.

choices.label: Where
choices.pinyin: Wǒ shì zài xuéxiào rènshi tā de.
choices.note: 在學校 is the detail in the spotlight.

choices.label: How
choices.pinyin: Wǒ shì shàngwǎng rènshi tā de.
choices.note: 上網 is the detail in the spotlight.

choices.label: With whom
choices.pinyin: Wǒ shì gēn tóngxué qù de.
choices.note: 跟同學 is the detail in the spotlight.

discoveryLab.takeaway: The event is known. Ask which detail should stand out.

examples.teachingNote: Inquiring about arrival time.

text.traditional:
A: 他已經到學校了。
B: 他是幾點到的？
A: 他是三點三十分到的。
text.simplified:
A: 他已经到学校了。
B: 他是几点到的？
A: 他是三点三十分到的。
text.pinyin:
A: Tā yǐjīng dào xuéxiào le.
B: Tā shì jǐ diǎn dào de?
A: Tā shì sān diǎn sānshí fēn dào de.
text.english:
A: He has already arrived at school.
B: What time did he arrive?
A: He arrived at 3:30.

examples.teachingNote: Inquiring about method of transportation.

text.traditional:
A: 張先生來了。
B: 他是開車來的嗎？
A: 不是，他是走路來的。
text.simplified:
A: 张先生来了。
B: 他是开车来的吗？
A: 不是，他是走路来的。
text.pinyin:
A: Zhāng xiānsheng lái le.
B: Tā shì kāichē lái de ma?
A: Bú shì, tā shì zǒulù lái de.
text.english:
A: Mr. Zhang has arrived.
B: Did he come by driving?
A: No, he came on foot.

examples.teachingNote: Inquiring about where an action took place.

text.traditional:
A: 你的中文說得真好，你是在哪裡學的？
B: 我在台灣學的。
text.simplified:
A: 你的中文说得真好，你是在哪里学的？
B: 我在台湾学的。
text.pinyin:
A: Nǐ de Zhōngwén shuō de zhēn hǎo, nǐ shì zài nǎlǐ xué de?
B: Wǒ zài Táiwān xué de.
text.english:
A: Your Chinese is really good! Where did you learn it?
B: I learned it in Taiwan.

examples.teachingNote: Inquiring about who did the action.

text.traditional:
A: 你知道她的手機號碼嗎？是誰告訴你的？
B: 是她媽媽告訴我的。
text.simplified:
A: 你知道她的手机号码吗？是谁告诉你的？
B: 是她妈妈告诉我的。
text.pinyin:
A: Nǐ zhīdào tā de shǒujī hàomǎ ma? Shì shéi gàosù nǐ de?
B: Shì tā māma gàosù wǒ de.
text.english:
A: Do you know her cell phone number? Who told you?
B: Her mother told me.

examples.teachingNote: Negative contrast with 是…的.

text.traditional: 他是昨天晚上到的，不是今天早上到的。
text.simplified: 他是昨天晚上到的，不是今天早上到的。
text.pinyin: Tā shì zuótiān wǎnshang dào de, bú shì jīntiān zǎoshang dào de.
text.english: He arrived yesterday evening, not this morning.

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.exerciseInstruction: Choose the 是…的 sentence that matches the clue.

questions.correctFeedback: 上網 comes before the known event 認識.
questions.repairFeedback: Put the detail before the action word.

segments.hint: Build 是 + detail + action word + 的.

questions.correctFeedback: 昨天 sits inside 是…的.
questions.repairFeedback: Build 是 + detail + action word + 的.

shì rènshi tā zài xuéxiào de

questions.correctFeedback: The place comes before 認識.
questions.repairFeedback: Put the place before the event.

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.titleEnglish: Tell 沒 and 還沒 Apart
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.learnerPromise: Distinguish between actions that did not happen in the past (沒) and actions that have not happened yet (還沒).
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.explanation: To say someone did not do an action in the past, use 沒 instead of 不. When an action hasn’t happened yet but you expect to do it later, use 還沒.

lessonWorld.title: Rebuild the chat history
lessonWorld.prompt: Yiwen asks whether Youmei has met her new friend.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我還沒決定要不要跟他見面。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我还没决定要不要跟他见面。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi juédìng yào bú yào gēn tā jiànmiàn.
lessonWorld.english: I have not yet decided whether to meet him.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.pattern: 否定過去動作：沒 ｜ 尚未發生：還沒

items.question: He did not come yesterday — 沒 or 還沒?
items.answer: 沒. Yesterday is finished, so the chance to come is over. 還沒 is for something still waiting to happen.

items.question: “I have not decided yet” — 還沒 or 還不?
items.answer: 還沒. 還不 sounds like you refuse. 還沒 says the decision has not happened up to now.

items.question: After 沒, do I keep the 了?
items.answer: No. 沒 already says it did not happen, so there is no finished action to mark. Drop 了.

right.english: I did not do the homework.

discoveryLab.title: Move the timeline to NOW
discoveryLab.description: 沒 says the event did not happen. 還沒 says it is still not done at this moment.

choices.label: Yesterday
choices.note: Yesterday is a finished time.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.note: The trip is still not done — up to now.

choices.label: Decision pending
choices.note: 還 adds the “up to now” meaning.

choices.label: Repair the negative
choices.traditional: 我沒有寫了功課 → 我沒有寫功課
choices.simplified: 我没有写了功课 → 我没有写功课
choices.pinyin: wǒ méiyǒu xiě le gōngkè → wǒ méiyǒu xiě gōngkè
choices.english: Remove 了 after negating the completed action.
choices.note: After 沒有, do not keep 了.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Use 還沒 when you mean “not yet.” After 沒有, do not keep 了.

text.traditional: A: 他昨天來了嗎？ B: 他昨天沒來。
text.simplified: A: 他昨天来了吗？ B: 他昨天没来。
text.pinyin: A: Tā zuótiān lái le ma? B: Tā zuótiān méi lái.
text.english: A: Did he come yesterday? B: He didn't come yesterday.

text.traditional: A: 他看書了沒有？ B: 他沒看書。
text.simplified: A: 他看书了没有？ B: 他没看书。
text.pinyin: A: Tā kànshū le méiyǒu? B: Tā méi kànshū.
text.english: A: Did he read the book? B: He didn't read the book.

text.traditional: A: 爸爸喝咖啡了沒？ B: 爸爸沒喝咖啡。

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that an action is finished.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 了 after the action word to show it is finished. When talking about amounts (like “two cups” or “ten pages”), a single 了 means you stopped there, while two 了’s mean you reached that amount so far and may keep going.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

items.question: Where does 了 go in “I wrote the homework yesterday”?
items.answer: Right after the action word. 了 follows 寫, before the homework.

items.question: Do I need 了 for something I do every day?
items.answer: No. 了 marks one finished action. For a habit you repeat, leave 了 out.

items.question: How do I say “I am writing a card” right now?
items.answer: Use 在 before the action word. 了 would say the card is already done.

discoveryLab.title: Watch the action reach DONE
discoveryLab.description: The picture—not the English time words—shows whether the action is happening now or already finished.

choices.label: General action
choices.note: The sentence names the activity. It does not say if it is happening now or finished.

choices.label: Happening now
choices.note: 在 shows the action is happening now.

choices.label: Completed
choices.note: 了 shows the action is finished.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Ask: is the action general, happening now, or finished?

examples.teachingNote: Single 了 after V(O) indicates a completed action in the past.

text.traditional: 他已經去上課了。
text.simplified: 他已经去上课了。
text.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng qù shàngkè le.

examples.teachingNote: 今天早上去看醫生了 indicates the visit is completed.

text.traditional: 我跟弟弟都寫功課了。
text.simplified: 我跟弟弟都写功课了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn dìdi dōu xiě gōngkè le.
text.english: My younger brother and I have both finished our homework.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for past completed quantity; (b) Double 了 indicates so far, with more likely to come.

text.traditional: 我上個禮拜學了十個中國字。我已經學了四百多個中國字了。
text.simplified: 我上个礼拜学了十个中国字。我已经学了四百多个中国字了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ shàng ge lǐbài xué le shí ge Zhōngguózì. Wǒ yǐjīng xué le sìbǎi duō ge Zhōngguózì le.
text.english: I learned ten Chinese characters last week. I have already learned more than 400 Chinese characters so far.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for buying a car; (b) Double 了 indicates he already bought one and still wants another.

text.traditional: 爸爸上個月買了一輛新車。爸爸已經買了一輛新車了，還想再買一輛。
text.simplified: 爸爸上个月买了一辆新车。爸爸已经买了一辆新车了，还想再买一辆。
text.pinyin: Bàba shàng ge yuè mǎi le yí liàng xīn chē. Bàba yǐjīng mǎi le yí liàng xīn chē le, hái xiǎng zài mǎi yí liàng.
text.english: Dad bought a new car last month. Dad has already bought a new car, and he still wants to buy another one.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for eating two apples yesterday; (b) Double 了 indicates he ate one so far and wants more.

items.question: He did not come yesterday — 沒 or 還沒?
items.answer: 沒. Yesterday is finished, so the chance to come is over. 還沒 is for something still waiting to happen.

items.question: After 沒, do I keep the 了?
items.answer: No. 沒 already says it did not happen, so there is no finished action to mark. Drop 了.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Spotlight One Detail with 是…的
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Point out when, where, how, or with whom something happened.
grammarPages.explanation: The event is already known. 是…的 puts the spotlight on one detail: when, where, how, or with whom it happened.

lessonWorld.title: Rebuild the chat history
lessonWorld.prompt: Yiwen knows that Youmei met someone. She wants the missing detail.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

grammarPages.pattern: Person + 是 + focused detail + action + 的

items.question: “How did you meet?” — do I answer with 了?
items.answer: No. The question asks how, so 是…的 puts the spotlight on the way you met. 了 alone would only say it happened.

items.question: Where does the detail go in a 是…的 sentence?
items.answer: Between 是 and the action word. The way you met comes before 認識.

items.question: Do I need the 的 at the end?
items.answer: Yes. 是…的 works as a pair. Without the ending 的, the sentence loses its spotlight.

discoveryLab.title: Move the spotlight
discoveryLab.description: The event stays known. Change only the detail the listener wants.

choices.label: With whom

discoveryLab.takeaway: The event is known. Ask which detail should stand out.

text.pinyin: Wǒmen shì shàngwǎng rènshi de, wǒ kàndào tā xiě de wénzhāng, ránhòu liúyán wèn le tā yí ge wèntí, tā huídá de hěn yǒuqù.
text.english: I met him on the net. I read his article on the internet, and then I left a question for him. His answer was interesting.

text.traditional: 你們常上網聊天嗎？
text.simplified: 你们常上网聊天吗？

text.simplified: 我还没决定。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi juédìng.
text.english: I haven’t decided.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Put Steps in Order with 先…等…再…
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Explain a plan where you do one thing, wait, then do another.
grammarPages.explanation: 先 starts the first action. 等 names what you wait for. 再 starts the later action.

lessonWorld.title: Plan what happens next
lessonWorld.prompt: Youmei needs to decide, wait for a free time, and then arrange the meeting.
lessonWorld.traditional: 先決定，等朋友有空，再約時間。
lessonWorld.simplified: 先决定，等朋友有空，再约时间。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Xiān juédìng, děng péngyǒu yǒukòng, zài yuē shíjiān.
lessonWorld.english: Decide first, wait until the friend is free, then arrange a time.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

grammarPages.pattern: 先 + first action，等 + condition，再 + later action

patternRows.english: Do homework first; wait for Dad; then eat.
Practice first; wait for the teacher; then start class.
Decide first; wait for the friend; then call.

items.question: Which step does 先 start?
items.answer: 先 starts the first action. 等 names what you wait for, and 再 starts the later action.

right.pinyin: Xiān zuò gōngkè, zài kàn diànshì.
right.english: Do homework first, then watch TV.

items.question: Is it 在 or 再 for the later step?
items.answer: 再. It means “then; after that”. 在 talks about where something is.

right.english: Decide first, then arrange a time.

items.question: Can 再 start the first step?
items.answer: No. 再 belongs to the later action. 先 opens the plan.

discoveryLab.title: Build the three-stop timeline
discoveryLab.description: Do not jump to 再. Something must happen or become true after 等.

choices.label: Dinner
choices.traditional: 先做功課，等爸爸回家，再一起吃飯。
choices.simplified: 先做功课，等爸爸回家，再一起吃饭。
choices.pinyin: Xiān zuò gōngkè, děng bàba huí jiā, zài yìqǐ chīfàn.
choices.english: Do homework first, wait for Dad to return, then eat together.
choices.note: The middle event must happen first.

choices.label: Class
choices.traditional: 先練習，等老師來了，再上課。
choices.simplified: 先练习，等老师来了，再上课。
choices.pinyin: Xiān liànxí, děng lǎoshī lái le, zài shàngkè.
choices.english: Practice first, wait for the teacher, then begin class.
choices.note: 老師來 is what you wait for after 等.

choices.label: Call later
choices.traditional: 先想一想，等妳決定了，再給我打電話。
choices.simplified: 先想一想，等你决定了，再给我打电话。
choices.pinyin: Xiān xiǎng yì xiǎng, děng nǐ juédìng le, zài gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
choices.english: Think first; when you decide, call me.
choices.note: The call waits for the decision.

discoveryLab.takeaway: 先 starts it. 等 waits for it. 再 moves to the later action.

examples.teachingNote: The first step is left out; the wait is named.

text.traditional: 等她睡醒了，再跟她說。
text.simplified: 等她睡醒了，再跟她说。
text.pinyin: Děng tā shuìxǐng le, zài gēn tā shuō.
text.english: Wait until she wakes, then tell her.

examples.teachingNote: What you wait for comes after 等.

text.traditional: 天氣太冷了，等車來了，我們再出去。
text.simplified: 天气太冷了，等车来了，我们再出去。
text.pinyin: Tiānqì tài lěng le, děng chē lái le, wǒmen zài chūqù.
text.english: It is too cold; wait for the car, then go outside.

examples.teachingNote: All three stages appear.

text.traditional: 先做功課，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯。
text.simplified: 先做功课，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚饭。
text.pinyin: Xiān zuò gōngkè, děng bàba huí jiā le, zài yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn.
text.english: Do homework first; when Dad returns, eat dinner together.

examples.teachingNote: A fun example from the book.

text.traditional: 我們先吃冰淇淋，等不熱了，再去海邊玩。
text.simplified: 我们先吃冰淇淋，等不热了，再去海边玩。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān chī bīngqílín, děng bú rè le, zài qù hǎibiān wán.
text.english: Let us eat ice cream first, wait until it is cooler, then go to the beach.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Send an Action to Someone with 給
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Show who receives a card, call, letter, or helpful action.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 給 before the person, then say the action. The action goes to that person.

lessonWorld.title: Send the action to someone
lessonWorld.prompt: Youmei writes a card to her new friend.
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gěi péngyǒu xiě kǎpiàn.
lessonWorld.english: I want to write a card to my friend.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

patternRows.english: I write a card to my friend.
Mom buys a gift for me.

items.question: “Write a card to a friend” — 給 or 跟?
items.answer: 給. The friend gets the card. 跟 goes with someone — like meeting or chatting together.

right.english: I write a card to my friend.

items.question: Where does the person who gets it go?
items.answer: Right after 給, before the action. 給 + person + action.

right.english: I write a card to my friend.

items.question: How do I say “my brother did not call me”?
items.answer: Put 給我 before 打電話. The person who gets the call comes right after 給.

right.pinyin: Gēge méi gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
right.english: My older brother did not call me.

discoveryLab.title: Follow the arrow to the person
discoveryLab.description: The action travels toward the person after 給.

choices.label: Friend
choices.english: I write a card to my friend.
choices.note: The friend gets the card.

choices.label: Me
choices.note: 我 gets the call.

choices.label: Mom
choices.english: I buy a gift for Mom.
choices.note: 媽媽 gets the gift.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Find who gets it. Put 給 right before that person.

examples.teachingNote: 她 gets the letter.

text.traditional: 我想給她寫信。
text.simplified: 我想给她写信。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gěi tā xiě xìn.
text.english: I want to write her a letter.

examples.teachingNote: Even after 沒, 給 stays before the person.

text.traditional: 哥哥沒給我打電話。
text.simplified: 哥哥没给我打电话。
text.pinyin: Gēge méi gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
text.english: My older brother did not call me.

examples.teachingNote: 我 gets the ice cream.

text.traditional: 媽媽給我買了冰淇淋。
text.simplified: 妈妈给我买了冰淇淋。
text.pinyin: Māma gěi wǒ mǎi le bīngqílín.
text.english: Mom bought me ice cream.

examples.teachingNote: You can use 還沒 and 給 together.

text.traditional: 你還沒給哥哥寫生日卡片嗎？
text.simplified: 你还没给哥哥写生日卡片吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ hái méi gěi gēge xiě shēngrì kǎpiàn ma?
text.english: Have you not written your brother a birthday card yet?

questions.correctFeedback: 給 comes before the person.

segments.hint: Use 給 + 我 + 打電話.

dialogue.title: 對話二 · Dialogue 2
dialogue.setting: 在教室裡 · In the classroom

text.traditional: 妳跟那位新朋友見面了沒有？
text.simplified: 妳跟那位新朋友见面了没有？
text.pinyin: Nǐ gēn nà wèi xīn péngyǒu jiànmiàn le méiyǒu?
text.english: Have you met up with your new friend yet?

text.traditional: 我還沒決定要不要跟他見面。
text.simplified: 我还没决定要不要跟他见面。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi juédìng yào bú yào gēn tā jiànmiàn.
text.english: I haven’t decided to meet him or not.

text.traditional: 妳擔心什麼？
text.simplified: 妳担心什么？
text.pinyin: Nǐ dānxīn shénme?
text.english: What are you worried about?

text.traditional: 我有點兒緊張，我以前沒有這種經驗，所以覺得這樣有點兒奇怪。
text.simplified: 我有点儿紧张，我以前没有这种经验，所以觉得这样有点儿奇怪。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎnr jǐnzhāng, wǒ yǐqián méiyǒu zhè zhǒng jīngyàn, suǒyǐ juéde zhèyàng yǒudiǎnr qíguài.
text.english: I am a little nervous. I have never had an experience like this before, so I think it is a little strange.

text.traditional: 妳不要緊張，我有辦法，我跟妳一起去。
text.simplified: 妳不要紧张，我有办法，我跟妳一起去。
text.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào jǐnzhāng, wǒ yǒu bànfǎ, wǒ gēn nǐ yìqǐ qù.
text.english: Don’t be nervous. I have an idea: I can be there for you.

text.traditional: 太好了，謝謝妳幫我的忙。
text.simplified: 太好了，谢谢妳帮我的忙。
text.pinyin: Tài hǎo le, xièxie nǐ bāng wǒ de máng.
text.english: Great! Thank you for helping me.

text.traditional: 不客氣。妳打算什麼時候跟他見面？
text.simplified: 不客气。妳打算什么时候跟他见面？
text.pinyin: Bú kèqi. Nǐ dǎsuàn shénme shíhou gēn tā jiànmiàn?
text.english: You’re welcome. When do you plan to meet him?

text.traditional: 可能這個週末吧。如果妳有空，我再跟他約時間。
text.simplified: 可能这个周末吧。如果妳有空，我再跟他约时间。
text.pinyin: Kěnéng zhège zhōumò ba. Rúguǒ nǐ yǒukòng, wǒ zài gēn tā yuē shíjiān.
text.english: Maybe this weekend. If you are free, I will arrange a time with him.

text.traditional: 有空啊，但是我明天不會來學校，等妳決定了，再給我打電話吧。
text.simplified: 有空啊，但是我明天不会来学校，等妳决定了，再给我打电话吧。
text.pinyin: Yǒukòng a, dànshì wǒ míngtiān bú huì lái xuéxiào, děng nǐ juédìng le, zài gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà ba.
text.english: I am free, but I won’t come to school tomorrow. When you decide, call me.
